summary:
FLAMEGUARD is an interactive data-driven platform designed to explore fire behavior and combustion safety in microgravity environments. Developed in response to NASA’s “Flame in Freefall” challenge, the project brings together experimental records from space-related fire research and terrestrial microgravity-relevant combustion studies.

The platform enables users to explore experimental conditions, examine data quality, compare matched experiments, investigate uncertainty, and identify patterns in combustion behavior through interactive visualizations. It also provides data exploration and CSV export capabilities to support further scientific analysis.

By making complex experimental information more accessible and interpretable, FLAMEGUARD aims to support research into spacecraft fire safety and contribute to a better understanding of combustion behavior under different environmental conditions.
details:
Project Overview

FLAMEGUARD is a computational research prototype designed to explore fire safety through the analysis of microgravity combustion data. It aims to bridge the gap between complex experimental datasets and accessible engineering insights.

How It Works

The platform uses a structured data-processing pipeline to organize and analyze combustion-related experimental data. Its architecture includes dedicated modules for data loading, configuration, analysis, and validation. NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) resources and combustion experiment datasets provide the scientific foundation for the project.

The application presents processed information through an interactive Streamlit dashboard, helping users explore experimental records, investigate combustion-related patterns, and understand the potential implications for spacecraft fire safety.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Fire behavior in microgravity can differ significantly from combustion under normal gravitational conditions. Understanding these differences is important for designing safer spacecraft and protecting astronauts during long-duration missions.

FLAMEGUARD provides a research-oriented environment for exploring available experimental evidence and supporting further investigation into microgravity fire safety.

Technologies and Tools

The project was developed using Python and Streamlit. Its modular architecture includes separate components for configuration, data loading, analysis, and validation. Git and GitHub were used for version control and project organization.

Creativity and Innovation

The project’s central idea is to connect experimental microgravity combustion research with an accessible computational analysis environment. Rather than presenting raw experimental information alone, FLAMEGUARD organizes the data into a structured workflow that can support scientific exploration and future development.

The project is a research prototype and is not intended to replace operational spacecraft fire detection or suppression systems.
